analysis:
Only scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py (an offline CI workflow test) changed. It contains no runtime provider, coordinator or crypto code, so the retained provider threat model (T-041 and others) is not directly affected. The test changes assert tighter CI behaviour:
- The restored .git validation (VALIDATE_GIT) now discards a cached .git that contains hooks, symlinks, core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath or include config, or is not a directory (head lines ~1065-1128). This tightens CI cache-poisoning defence. I checked that the test plants these unsafe cases and asserts that nothing executes, which is a correct negative test.
- Every actions/cache step must be gated by CACHE_GATE so that a Darkbloom Sandbox without a cache URL does not read or write GitHub's cache (head lines 1336-1407).
- Cache saves are limited to pushes on master/dev, caches live under CI_CACHE_ROOT, and checkouts keep persist-credentials: false (lines ~968-1063).
These tests make the CI controls stricter, with no regression or new attack surface in this file. A remaining gap I could not verify: the actual workflow, action and script files that these assertions cover (such as the VALIDATE_GIT script and the cache-gate step) are not in the supplied units. The tests only help if those files really implement the controls. The find/grep-based hook and config detection also has inherent limits, for example config keys written in unusual forms. The patch excerpt is truncated, so unseen portions of the file were not reviewed. Any security conclusion about the CI hardening itself depends on reviewing the non-test files.
